title: Portugal, Slovakia and Norway join cross-border initiative on autonomous vehicle testbeds
source_name: 欧盟委员会交通与运输总司
content: Today, Portugal, Slovakia and Norway signed the Joint Declaration of Intent on large-scale cross-border testbeds for autonomous vehicles during Connecting Europe Days in Brussels. Spain signed the Declaration last week, bringing the total number of participating countries to 22. The additional signatories reflect the continued commitment to accelerate the harmonised deployment of autonomous vehicles across Europe in a safe, coordinated and competitive way, building on the initiative launched under the European Automotive Action Plan. Background The large-scale cross-border testbed initiative for autonomous vehicles was launched under the European Automotive Action Plan. It aims to support the harmonised commercial pre-deployment of autonomous vehicles across Europe by bringing together Member States, non-EU countries, regional and local authorities, industry stakeholders and transport operators. The Joint Declaration was first signed in June by 18 Member States. Spain joined the initiative last week, followed today by Portugal, Slovakia and Norway, bringing the total number of participating countries to 22. - Publication date - 29 September 2026 - Author - Directorate-General for Mobility and Transport

title: Danube Transport Ministers renew push for effective waterway rehabilitation and maintenance
source_name: 欧盟委员会交通与运输总司
content: The Danube Ministers of Transport have today renewed their commitment to rehabilitating and maintaining the Danube and its navigable tributaries, stressing the river’s vital role for Europe’s transport network and crisis resilience. In the adopted Ministerial Conclusions, the Ministers of nine Danube riparian countries (Austria, Bulgaria, Croatia, Germany, Moldova, Romania, Serbia, Slovakia, Ukraine) called for closer cooperation between waterway authorities, the navigation sector and environmental stakeholders across the region. They underlined the growing need for reliable, resilient and environmentally sustainable waterways as hydrological conditions become more challenging. The Danube is a key part of the Rhine-Danube Core Network Corridor and has proved its strategic value in recent years, including through the EU-Ukraine Solidarity Lanes. The Ministers reaffirmed the goal of achieving Good Navigation Status on the Danube, its canals and navigable tributaries that are part of the TEN-T network by 2030, while ensuring full compliance with environmental legislation and support for the river’s ecological functions. They also highlighted the importance of the Fairway Rehabilitation and Maintenance Master Plan, which has guided coordinated action across the region since 2014. At the same time, Ministers acknowledged that progress remains uneven and that droughts, floods and other extreme weather events are increasing the pressure on navigation. They called for proactive maintenance, stronger cooperation and more flexible solutions, including low-flow navigation channels, adaptable infrastructure and nature-based approaches. By reaffirming their joint commitment, the Danube Ministers of Transport have sent a clear signal: securing the Danube’s future requires coordinated action, long-term investment and a balanced approach that supports both navigation and environmental sustainability. - Publication date - 29 September 2026 - Author - Directorate-General for Mobility and Transport
